stem: Why should source-water identity be verified before comparing two fertigation batches?
choices: Source water can be ignored if both final batches reach the same EC and pH targets.
Source identity matters mainly when total dissolved solids differ enough to change the starting EC by more than the meter tolerance.
Different source-water alkalinity and ionic composition can change pH behavior, nutrient contribution, and how two otherwise similar fertigation batches should be interpreted.
Source-water identity matters primarily for outdoor or recirculating systems because controlled indoor recipes override normal source variation.
rationale: Source water contributes its own alkalinity and dissolved ions to the final solution. Two batches can be prepared from the same recipe yet respond differently to acid/base adjustment or contribute different background ions when the source water changes. Verifying source identity therefore helps explain pH behavior, nutrient contribution, and batch-to-batch differences that final EC alone may not reveal.
